messages:
Maya: Hi team — customer acme-mobile is hitting intermittent 403s after we rotated their mobile ephemeral API key this morning. They say ~20% of requests fail immediately after the rollout and recover after ~2–4 minutes. Repro steps and logs below, paging infra/edge and eng-sre.
Maya: Repro (from their report):
- Rotate key via dashboard
- Mobile clients get new key via SDK sync
- Some clients 403 on first call, then 200 on retry

Maya: Example client error: 
```
POST /v1/generate 403 Forbidden
{ error: 'API key revoked' }
```

Maya: Their SDK sends header like: -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral-token>'

Maya: They also provided an edge log snippet showing immediate 403s with the revoked key fingerprint: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2067001205 GET /v1/generate 403 key=fingerprint-abc123 revoked=true route=edge-eu
```

oncall-bot: Rotation job ran: 2067001200 by job/rotate-ephemeral-keys (ok) :information_source:

Jason: Noted. Did the rotation job revoke the old key immediately or mark it pending? If we revoke immediately but the edge cache still holds the old key mapping, requests using the old token will be rejected by vault check but edge might not refresh mapping until cache TTL expires.

Liam: I dug into the rotation script. It does two things in order: 1) revoke token in Vault (kv v2), 2) publish key-update event to kafka topic 'keys.fanout'. There's an intentional publish, but I see a couple of worker logs showing consumer lag at the time of the job (SQS consumer backlog ~120s). So edge listeners might have seen the event late.

Sophie: Also important: the mobile SDK rotates and hits our edge directly. The edge has an in-memory key->account mapping that is updated only after the key-update event is processed. We also have a 5min LRU cache for key lookups at the sidecar to reduce latency. If the token is revoked before consumers invalidate caches, clients will get 403s until the cache entry falls out or the fanout processes.

Maya: Customer reported that retries succeed after ~2–4 minutes which matches either cache TTL or consumer lag. They lost a release window. They asked for immediate mitigation and a postmortem.

Jason: For immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) publish a 'soft-revoke' flag instead of full revoke (mark key pending) so existing in-flight cached entries still validate for X seconds, 2) force-clear edge caches for the affected key(s). Can infra run an invalidate for fingerprint-abc123 now?

Liam: I can run targeted invalidates and also kick the kafka consumer to catch up. Running edgectl now: 
```
edgectl invalidate --key fingerprint-abc123 --region eu
```

infra-bot: edgectl job queued (job-id: 2067001242), targeting edge-eu nodes.

Liam: Done, also bumped consumer workers from 3->6 to drain backlog. Observed consumers caught up within ~40s.

Sophie: After invalidation and consumer drain, customer confirms errors dropped to 0 and retries succeed immediately. Good.

Maya: Root cause summary hypothesis: rotation pipeline revoked keys before edge/sidecar caches and consumer fans had processed the update, producing a narrow race (revoke -> cache still had mapping -> queries fail). The short-lived nature made it appear intermittent depending on which node handled the request.

Jason: Action items (immediate):
- Add a 60s 'grace' state in rotation where key is marked 'revoking' but still accepted by edge cache until fanout confirmed. (owner: eng-sre)
- Make rotation publish-and-wait: rotation job should publish event and wait for consumer acknowledgement (or timeout) before final revoke. (owner: infra)
- Add targeted cache-invalidate API call to rotation orchestrator so we call edgectl as part of the workflow. (owner: eng-platform)
- Incident comms to acme-mobile + offer credits. (owner: support)

Sophie: Longer term: decreasing sidecar cache TTL from 5m->30s for ephemeral keys; making edge perform a quick failover check to remote auth when local cache entry returns revoked (instead of hard 403) for ephemeral class tokens; and exposing rotation dry-run mode to test pipeline. (owners: eng-runtime + eng-platform)

Liam: Quick repro steps for engineers:
1) Run rotation job in staging: ./scripts/rotate-ephemeral --dry-run --env staging
2) Simulate consumer lag: kafka-consumer-slowdown --topic keys.fanout --delay 90s
3) Send requests to edge nodes with old token and confirm 403 window replicates

Maya: Customer followup message drafted. Will send after confirming fixes in staging.

Jason: I'll file a postmortem template and link the logs + offsets. Also we should add a short blurb in docs about ephemeral key rotation semantics for mobile SDKs.

Maya: Thanks all. Please add any missing steps. :thumbsup:
